title: Measuring the Marginal Coverage of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding automated sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for intent→configuration artifacts produced by a declared model (gpt-5-mini, provider recorded as openai_responses). Using shared_initial_candidate semantics we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results are far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (20 percentage points). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, a concise explanation of provider-call audit fields, an artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded effect in this regime, and prescriptive boundary conditions for when sandboxed emulation is likely to add operational value.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for intent-driven NetOps tasks such as translating operator intent into device configuration. Operational deployment requires outputs that satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow ordering, and policy/invariant constraints. A common practical architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to exercise runtime behaviors that static validators cannot capture. Surveys and system reports advocate such layered workflows but provide limited paired, preregistered measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed emulation when the same generated candidate is analyzed by both conditions. Motivated by that gap, we preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study to measure the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation, under shared_initial_candidate semantics.
sections.related_work: Prior work documents two relevant trends. First, architecture and survey papers emphasize workflow-centred mitigation: combine generation with deterministic validators, verifiers, and repair loops to raise assurance for configuration artifacts [1], and prototype systems augment static checking with emulation to reveal runtime-only failures [2]. Second, empirical studies from program-verification and NetOps-adjacent domains show that LLMs can produce incorrect or hallucinated outputs and that external verifiers or simulation harnesses often improve correctness in targeted regimes [3], though gains depend strongly on task distribution and validator coverage. Our study provides a preregistered, artifact-grounded datapoint that isolates downstream guarded-stage contributions by reusing the same initial generation across paired conditions (shared_initial_candidate), complementing the descriptive prior literature with a controlled paired estimate.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We froze a paired-binary confirmatory plan before execution (study_id above). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Planned Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). Minimum effect-of-interest for power planning = 0.20. Inclusion/exclusion, deterministic reseed rules for parser failures, multiplicity handling, contamination controls, and analysis procedures were specified in the preregistration.

Task bank and vendor abstractions. Confirmatory items were deterministically generated from the intent_configuration_repair_v1 family. The bank spans three abstract vendor‑CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest contains initial/final states, an explicit intent, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (make-before-break, must-be-down-for-fields, group activity constraints). Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; no irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred in the confirmatory run (complete pairs = 720).

Model, generation semantics, and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses). The client did not supply an explicit temperature (recorded as null in the model configuration); this does not imply provider-side determinism. For each pair we obtained exactly one sampled initial candidate (one provider call) and the identical candidate was analyzed by both conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). This isolates downstream guarded-stage signals (emulation observations or repair) as the sole source of between-condition discordance.

Baseline validator. The baseline is deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Its checks include vendor-CLI syntactic parsing and canonicalization; per-command parsing; sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence; atomicity/workflow constraints; protected-interface and group-level invariants; and final-state conformance tests. The validator emits a binary detection flag under the preregistered scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation and a validator_trace object documenting parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validation_before/after, violation_codes, and normalized_configuration.

Guarded pipeline and sandboxed emulator. The guarded pipeline runs the baseline validator and then executes the candidate in an automated sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and applies normalized CLI commands to vendor-abstracted virtual devices. The harness records runtime observations (interface admin transitions, transient concurrency states, MTU/VLAN application, and topology-level connectivity) and maps those observations to runtime-observation rules that can trigger additional detections not encoded in the static validator rule set. Mapping from emulation observations to guarded detections was intentionally conservative.

Repair policy and provider-call accounting. The preregistered repair policy permitted at most one repair‑stage model call per task, invoked only after initial generation and downstream observations were available for the guarded condition. Provider-call auditing records stage-level counts (see Provider-call audit clarification below). In the confirmatory execution the run accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1.

Provider-call audit clarification. The execution manifest contains a provider_call_audit object that reports model-call counts by instrumentation stage. "shared_initial_generation" counts initial model calls whose outputs were shared across both paired conditions (one per task under shared_initial_candidate semantics). "repair" or any other guarded-stage stage counts model calls fired only in the guarded branch (e.g., repair invocations). A small condition_counts summary in the audit may label calls by their stage association (e.g., "shared":720, "guarded":1) but those labels reflect stage association rather than per-condition detection outcomes; they do not imply that 720 model calls were confined to a single experimental arm. This distinction resolves the apparent mismatch between episode accounting and audited model-call labels and shows why completed_episode_count = 1440 and model_calls_used = 721 are consistent with shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Analysis procedures. The primary analysis used a paired-binary executor aligned with McNemar-style inference and cluster-robust variance estimation. We report exact McNemar two-sided p-values and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile confidence interval (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) as preregistered. Secondary per-class and per-vendor paired analyses were prespecified as exploratory with Bonferroni-adjusted intervals; no secondary contrasts produced notable discordance in this confirmatory run.
sections.results:
Confirmed paired outcomes (artifact-grounded). Summary contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Complete_pair_count = 720; completed_episode_count = 1440; failed_episode_count = 0. Model_calls_used = 721 (shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1).

Discordant-pair attribution. Because we enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics, any guarded-only detection must originate downstream of generation: either (i) a guarded-emulation runtime observation that the validator's rule set did not encode, or (ii) the single recorded repair-stage model invocation. Provider-call audit and reconciliation artifacts confirm exactly one repair-stage call and a single n10 discordant count. The archived per-episode raw results and validator/emulation traces map that unique discordant pair_id to the recorded repair-stage call (these per-episode artifacts are part of the canonical archived execution bundle). Representative validator_trace excerpts from multiple episodes show parsed_command_count and required_command_count equal and violation_count = 0 in the vast majority of confirmatory items, consistent with the high baseline success rate.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded interpretation. Three artifact-supported factors explain the negligible aggregate guarded benefit in this experimental regime. First, a validator-ceiling effect: the validator explicitly encoded the workflow constraints that the curated tasks exercised (e.g., shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break patterns). The baseline success rate was 719/720, leaving virtually no headroom for emulation to add detections. Second, curated inclusion reduced adversarial exposure: tasks required parser acceptance prior to inclusion, producing a narrow distribution of parser-validated, policy-constrained inputs that favor the static validator. Third, the shared_initial_candidate design and minimal repair activity (one repair call) constrain discordance sources to a single documented downstream event; provider-call auditing confirms this account.

Operational implications. For environments with high-coverage static validators tailored to constrained, parser-validated intent distributions, automated sandboxed emulation may deliver little incremental detection benefit relative to its cost. Conversely, when inputs are noisier or adversarial, or when validator coverage is intentionally narrower (e.g., due to latency constraints or unknown vendor diversity), guarded sandboxing can reveal runtime semantics and side-effects that static rules miss. Practitioners should thus consider a conditional deployment strategy: invest in richer static validators for high-throughput, low-latency pipelines, and reserve guarded sandboxing for high-risk changes, adversarial testing, or when validator coverage cannot be expanded.

Limitations rooted in the archived evidence. The finding is narrowly scoped to the preregistered task bank, the single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), the declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini), and shared_initial_candidate semantics. The study was powered a priori to detect a minimum paired difference of 0.20; the observed estimate (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as evidence of a near-zero effect in this constrained regime rather than general proof that guarded stages are unnecessary. Emulation fidelity and broader vendor/OS diversity—both limited in our harness—could produce different outcomes in other regimes. Residual provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain possible although the execution manifest includes deterministic reconciliation and provider-call auditing to reduce such concerns.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired study to quantify the marginal detection benefit of sandboxed emulation when paired with a strong deterministic validator on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting (completed_episode_count = 1440, model_calls_used = 721, repair calls = 1) and deterministic reconciliation show the single guarded-only detection maps to a documented downstream event. The evidence supports a conditional conclusion: where validators closely match the expected task distribution and inputs are parser-validated, guarded sandboxing may add little incremental coverage; guarded stages retain value in adversarial, noisy, or production-diverse settings. The archived execution and analysis artifacts provide reproducible seeds for adversarial follow-up experiments and for evaluating increased emulator fidelity.

Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the autonomous pipeline performed literature selection, preregistration, code and prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting without manual human editing of technical manuscript content.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove potential between-condition generation variability; this constrains discordance sources to downstream observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding rather than a universal negative result.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the archived execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts.
